claims.claim: **Assess pain regularly and after every intervention; combine non-drug and drug methods; use a graded drug approach.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Undertreated pain has lasting effects** on the child's experience of pain and later medical encounters, and can harm healing and development.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pain can make a child very quiet.** Reassess behaviour, physiology and pain after the predicted onset of each drug.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pain tools:** FPS-R 3–18 years (self-rated); numeric rating scale over 7 years (self-rated); NIPS under 3 months (clinician); FLACC 2 months to 7 years (clinician, score 0–10); revised FLACC for all non-verbal children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Constant pain: prescribe regularly, not PRN.** Give paracetamol and ibuprofen together where appropriate. **Use opioids early for moderate to severe pain.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Injuries:** splint or backslab suspected fractures immediately, ice (if age appropriate) and elevate, dress burns promptly, and consider a regional nerve block for limb or finger injuries.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infants:** swaddling, feeding, skin-to-skin care and a dummy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Topical anaesthetic eye drops are for examination only — they interfere with healing.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe acute ear pain:** short-term topical 2% lignocaine or Auralgan®, 1–2 drops, **only onto an intact tympanic membrane**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sucrose (any concentration, e.g. 24%, 33%) orally per procedure:** preterm (32–40 weeks corrected) 0.2–0.5 mL; under 1 month 0.5–1 mL; 1–18 months 1–2 mL. Daily max: preterm 2.5 mL; under 3 months 5 mL; 3 months and over 10 mL. Give a quarter of the dose to the anterior tongue 2 minutes before the procedure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Paracetamol** (dose on ideal body weight; oral preferred). **Oral:** 15 mg/kg (max 1 g) every 4–6 hours; daily max birth–1 month 60 mg/kg; over 1 month 90 mg/kg (max 4 g) for severe pain for up to 48 hours, then 60 mg/kg/day. **Rectal:** 15–20 mg/kg (max 1 g) every 6 hours, same daily limits; absorption delayed and erratic; avoid in immunocompromised children. **IV:** under 1 month 10 mg/kg every 6 hours (max 40 mg/kg/day); over 1 month 15 mg/kg every 6 hours (max 1 g a dose; 60 mg/kg/day, max 4 g). ⚠️ **mg/mL mix-ups have led to significant overdoses in young children.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ibuprofen orally, over 3 months:** 10 mg/kg every 6–8 hours (max 400 mg), with food; max 30 mg/kg/day (max 2.4 g). Caution in renal impairment, dehydration, bleeding or anticoagulation. **Asthma is not a contraindication.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oxycodone orally:** 1–12 months 0.05–0.1 mg/kg every 4 hours (max 0.6 mg/kg/day); over 12 months 0.1–0.2 mg/kg (adult 5–10 mg) every 4 hours (max 1.2 mg/kg/day). Short-term use; **do not prescribe for outpatients without a clear diagnosis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Morphine IV/subcut:** under 1 month 0.025 mg/kg; 1–12 months 0.05 mg/kg; over 12 months ≤0.2 mg/kg, capped at 5–10 mg. Cumulative max: under 1 month 0.1 mg/kg every 4–6 hours (0.6 mg/kg a day); 1–12 months 0.1 mg/kg every 2–4 hours (1.2 mg/kg a day); over 12 months 0.2 mg/kg every 2–4 hours (2.4 mg/kg a day).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intranasal fentanyl, over 12 months:** first dose 1.5 microg/kg (max 100 microg), then 0.75 microg/kg after 10 minutes; total 3 microg/kg/day; split between nostrils by atomiser. **Not recommended under 12 months.** Consider other ongoing analgesia after the second dose.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tramadol oral/IV, over 12 years:** 0.5–1 mg/kg every 6 hours (max 100 mg); max 4 mg/kg/day (max 400 mg); up to 2 mg/kg if no sleep-apnoea or respiratory-depression risk. ⚠️ **Avoid in epilepsy and in young people on SSRIs.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Never give opioids as the sole analgesic** — combine with regular simple analgesia. Consider causes of ongoing severe pain such as **compartment syndrome**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Renal impairment:** prefer fentanyl over morphine, reduce oxycodone dose and frequency, and watch for opioid accumulation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Opioid toxicity:** airway support, oxygen, assist ventilation; **naloxone 10 microg/kg (max 400 microg) IM or IV**, then **100 microg/kg (max 2 mg)** if no response. Repeat doses may be needed for long-acting opioids.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prescribing:** involve the GP for courses over 1 week; keep courses short; **prescribe aperients with ongoing opioids**; check safe-prescribing databases before prescribing opioids.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the paediatric team** if analgesia is inadequate despite a regular oral/IV regimen. **Discharge** when pain or distress is managed and anticipated pain has been planned for.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute pain management' (Last updated October 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_pain_management/, retrieved 2026-09-23
